attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. The OpenAI sentence that "Same thing" refers back to is also his.

semantics.note: Faithfully keeps the broad scope and the claim about his books. "Hardly seems ethical" is a normative opinion, not a condition, so it is not scored.

contract.note: Fair plain reading. Requiring title-level evidence for the claim about his books is reasonable because Marcus did not name the books. Reading "ripped off" as unauthorized copying, not necessarily infringement, matches his words.

evidence.note: The June 2025 court order establishes broad training on copyrighted books and that pirated library copies were not fair use. This supports the general part. It does not identify any of Marcus's books.

reviews.rationale: The court order supports the general claim that Anthropic took in copyrighted material, pirated books included. The support condition also needs title-level evidence that Marcus's books were copied or used, and the packet has none; the settlement lookup could not be inspected. Nothing contradicts either part. Because the conjunctive claim is not settled, the outcome is unresolved, with the general part supported.

attribution.note: The judgment that the prediction is not remotely plausible is Marcus's own. The Amodei prediction is his paraphrase and serves as context, not as his claim.

semantics.note: "Not remotely plausible" expresses near-certainty that AGI will not arrive by the end of Amodei's window. The drafter's modality, "unlikely", understates that commitment. The horizon and the limit to original definitions are kept.

contract.note: Reading AGI as broad human-level competence is an ordinary reading of "original definitions". The August 31, 2026 deadline is a fair way to resolve a month-level date. The result still depends on a definition Marcus did not specify.

evidence.note: The 2023 transcript shows Amodei's threshold was narrower (an hour of conversation) and conditional. This bears on Marcus's paraphrase, not on whether AGI arrived.
A May 2026 preprint saying no measurement framework exists. It does not show whether any system met AGI.
ARC results dated before the deadline show strong benchmark progress, including 30% on ARC-AGI-3. These benchmarks are not a full test of broad competence.

reviews.rationale: The deadline passed on August 31, 2026. The packet has no independent evaluation showing that broad human-level AGI was met (contradiction) or was not met under a specified historical definition (support). The benchmark results show progress but do not settle either side, and the preprint confirms there is no agreed measure. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own characterization. The quoted fundraising speech is his paraphrase, not words he attributes to Altman or Amodei verbatim.

semantics.note: Keeps "over and over" and "basically amounting to". "Hype" is evaluative. The fundraising link is Marcus's interpretation of what their talk implies.

contract.note: Splitting the claim into repeated warnings plus a link to resources is a fair plain reading. "Basically amounting to" is interpretive, so whether communications must show an explicit link determines the result.

evidence.note: Both men signed the 2023 extinction-risk statement. Supports the warning component only.
Altman's 2015 essay calls superhuman AI the greatest threat to humanity. With e1, it shows he repeated the warning.
Amodei's January 2026 essay repeats civilization-scale risks and argues development can't stop. It supports the warnings and only partly a speed argument. It does not ask for money.
OpenAI's financing announcement gives demand as its rationale, not apocalyptic risk. It cannot exclude other pitches.
Anthropic's Series G announcement links funding to infrastructure and demand. It shows they sought resources, not that the pitch rested on fear.

reviews.rationale: The warning component holds: dated records show repeated catastrophic-risk warnings from both men before March 2026. The packet does not establish that their communications used those warnings to obtain money for faster development. The financing announcements cite demand, though that does not refute the claim. With the link part unsettled, the outcome is unresolved.

attribution.note: The core assertion is Marcus's own. The quoted All-In Podcast passage is someone else's words and is not part of the claim.

semantics.note: The firm core (targeting use before and after the dispute) is kept. "Presumably" consent and "likely" assistance are hedged and correctly recorded as qualifiers, so they are not scored.

contract.note: A fair reading. Counting assistance with identifying or prioritizing targets as "targeting" matches ordinary use, and the hedged clauses are treated separately.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure from February 2026: Claude is extensively deployed for intelligence analysis and operational planning. It does not mention targeting.

Guardian report: Claude remained in use after the ban announcement, in an article on AI targeting. It supports continued use after the dispute, but the excerpt does not tie Claude to targeting. The available_at date lags the article date.

reviews.rationale: The evidence supports deployment and continued use after the dispute. It does not document Claude-assisted targeting before the dispute, and the excerpt does not tie Claude specifically to targeting after it; the key Washington Post report could not be read. Nothing contradicts the claim. The hedged consent and assistance clauses are not scored. Unresolved.
